get.description:
Return the current authenticated user's profile and subscription tier.

Side effect: issues the ``fixmytext_session`` cookie. The browser stores it
HttpOnly + host-only, and from this request onward the cookie is sufficient
for authentication on subsequent requests (Bearer JWT is still accepted in
parallel for the transition window — see ``get_current_user``).

post.description:
Re-send the Keycloak email-verification email to the current user.

Backs the in-app "Verify your email" banner. With the realm's blocking
verify-email requirement disabled, Keycloak no longer emails at signup or
on login — this endpoint (and the first-login send in ``deps.py``) is how
verification links reach the user. No-op for already-verified users.

Clear the per-app session cookie. Called by the frontend on logout
BEFORE redirecting to Keycloak's end-session endpoint.

No auth required — clearing is idempotent. As a side effect the current
session is added to the Redis revocation set so it cannot be replayed
even if the browser ignores the Max-Age=0 instruction.

delete.description:
Soft-delete all history entries for the authenticated user.

Sets ``is_deleted=True`` on every non-deleted row rather than physically
removing data, preserving audit trail and enabling future undo.

get.description:
Return a paginated list of the user's operation history (newest first).

Soft-deleted entries are excluded.  Optionally filter by ``tool_id``.

post.description:
Record a new text-transformation operation in the user's history.

Input and output previews are truncated to ``PREVIEW_MAX`` characters to
avoid bloating the history table.

get.description:
Return a summary of the user's operation history.

Uses a single grouped query that fetches per-tool count **and**
last-used timestamp in one database round-trip.  The ``recent_tools``
list is derived from the same result set by sorting on ``last_used``
instead of issuing a separate query.  Soft-deleted entries are excluded.

delete.description:
Soft-delete a single history entry for the authenticated user.

Marks the row as deleted rather than physically removing it, consistent
with the bulk ``clear_history`` endpoint.

get.description:
Retrieve a single history entry by ID for the authenticated user.

Returns 404 if the entry does not exist, belongs to another user, or
has been soft-deleted.

post.description:
Create a shareable link for a transformed result.

Authentication is optional -- anonymous visitors may also create shares.
The output text is truncated to ``MAX_SHARE_TEXT_LENGTH`` characters.

get.description:
View a shared result by its public ID.

No authentication required.  Returns 410 Gone if the share has passed
the ``SHARE_EXPIRE_DAYS`` window.
Return paginated list of tools the authenticated user has discovered.
Return the authenticated user's favorited tools sorted by display order.

post.description:

get.description: Return all of the authenticated user's tool groups in display order.

post.description:
Create a named tool group, optionally pre-filled with tools.

Idempotent by name: if the user already has a group with this name, the
existing group is returned unchanged (200) — tool_ids are NOT merged in.
This keeps guest-adoption retries and double-clicked starter-kit cards
from erroring or duplicating.

put.description:
Reorder the authenticated user's tool groups.

Groups listed in `group_ids` get sort_order = array position; the user's
remaining groups keep their relative order after the listed ones. Unknown
and foreign ids are ignored. Idempotent — resending the same list is a
no-op. Returns all groups in the new display order.

delete.description: Delete a tool group (and its items) owned by the authenticated user.

put.description: Rename a tool group owned by the authenticated user.

Replace a group's tools with an explicit ordered list.

Array position becomes sort_order, so a single call covers drag-reorder,
bulk add, and bulk remove. Duplicates keep their first position.
Idempotent — resending the current list is a no-op.

delete.description: Remove a tool from one of the authenticated user's groups.

post.description:
Add a tool to one of the authenticated user's groups.

Idempotent: returns the existing entry if the tool is already in the group.

get.description: Return aggregated tool usage statistics for the authenticated user.
Return the authenticated user's UI settings (tool view, keybindings, panel sizes).

put.description: Update the authenticated user's UI settings (partial update).

get.description: Return the authenticated user's active passes and total credit balance.

Return all available passes and credit packs with regional pricing.

Auto-detects region from the client's IP address if not provided or invalid.

post.description: Claim a referral code, granting rewards to both the referrer and the new user.

Create a Razorpay order for purchasing a credit pack.

Resolves the user's region and returns a Razorpay order with pricing
in the correct currency.

Create a Razorpay order for purchasing a pass.

Resolves the user's region (from explicit param, stored value, or IP),
then creates a Razorpay order with the correct regional pricing.

get.description: Get or generate the authenticated user's unique referral code and URL.

post.description: Spin the weekly reward wheel for a random prize (pass or credits).

Verify a Razorpay payment signature, then grant the purchased pass or credits.

Fulfillment is idempotent and exactly-once: this verify callback and the
Razorpay webhook converge on a single ledger keyed by the payment id, so a
replayed body or a verify/webhook race grants the entitlement only once.
Tool scope and the paid amount are validated server-side against the order
notes and the catalog — the client-supplied ``tool_ids`` are ignored.

Cancel Pro. Access continues until the paid period ends (expires_at).

Idempotent: cancelling an already-cancelled in-period plan returns the
same response without changing anything.
Create a Razorpay order for upgrading to Pro (one-time monthly payment).

get.description: Return the current user's subscription status, usage, and pass/credit info.

post.description:
Verify Razorpay payment and activate Pro.

Trust model:
  1. The client-supplied signature is verified against Razorpay's servers.
  2. The order is re-fetched from Razorpay's API (server-to-server) and the
     ``notes.user_id`` embedded at order-creation time is compared to the
     authenticated user.  These notes originate from *our* backend (set in
     ``create_pro_checkout``), not from the client request, so they are
     trustworthy once the order ID is confirmed authentic.

Handle Razorpay webhook events for payments.

Supports: payment.captured, payment.authorized, payment.failed,
subscription.cancelled, subscription.halted.

Idempotent — duplicate events (same razorpay_event_id) are acknowledged
but not reprocessed.

Check (and consume) a tool entitlement for a user or anonymous visitor.

Returns 200 with ``allowed=false`` for quota-exhausted (the caller decides
UX), 422 for malformed input, 401 for a bad internal secret, and 503 if the
database is unavailable (callers fail closed for paid tools on 503).

get.description:
Poll the status of an enqueued AI job.

Status values: ``queued``, ``in_progress``, ``complete``, ``failed``, ``not_found``.
``result`` is populated (with ``original``, ``result``, ``operation``) when status is ``complete``.

post.description:
Execute an AI text transformation tool.

All registered AI tools are available here.  Parameterised tools
(translate, change-tone, change-format) expect additional fields in
the request body.

Enqueue an AI tool job for async execution via arq worker.

Returns immediately with a ``job_id``. Poll ``GET /jobs/{job_id}`` for the result.
Useful for tools where Groq latency would block the ASGI worker.

Stream AI tool output via Server-Sent Events (token-by-token).

Returns a ``text/event-stream`` response. Only available for registered
AI tools.
